article.Citation/Title: Bogenschutz, M. P., Forcehimes, A. A., Pommy, J. A., Wilcox, C. E., Barbosa, P. C. R., & Strassman, R. J. (2015). Psilocybin-assisted treatment for alcohol dependence: A proof-of-concept study. Journal of Psychopharmacology, 29(3), 289-299.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Psilocybin-assisted treatment for alcohol dependence - A proof-of-concept study (Bogenschutz et al., 2015) (1).pdf
article.InterventionDescription: Oral psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg then up to 0.4 mg/kg), two 8-hour supervised sessions at weeks 4 and 8, embedded in 12-week Motivational Enhancement Therapy plus preparation/debriefing sessions.

ae_events.Description: Mild headache, resolved within 24 hours following psilocybin administration.
Nausea with one episode of emesis during a psilocybin session.
Diarrhea during a psilocybin session in a participant with pre-existing irritable bowel syndrome.
Insomnia on the night following a psilocybin session.

article.Outcome: Statistical analysis section names the primary drinking outcome as percent heavy drinking days with primary contrast baseline vs. weeks 5-12. Results, 'Clinical outcomes': 'Percent heavy drinking days decreased during weeks 5-12 relative to baseline (mean difference (SD) = 26.0 (22.4), 95% CI 8.7-43.2, t(8) = 3.477, p = 0.008).' Used this combined-window mean difference rather than the per-sub-window Cohen's d values in Figure 3 (which split the same span into weeks 5-8 and weeks 9-12 separately and are embedded in an OCR-garbled image-derived table), because the text explicitly designates the combined baseline-vs-weeks-5-12 contrast as primary and no single Figure-3 value corresponds to exactly that window.
article.SD: t(8) = 3.477, the paired-samples t-statistic reported in the same sentence as Outcome, for the identical baseline-vs-weeks-5-12 contrast (Results, 'Clinical outcomes'). The raw SD of the mean difference (22.4) is given in the same sentence and is used in Retention/SampleSize reasoning but the t-statistic (with df) was chosen for this field since it is the inferential statistic paired with the effect and carries the degrees of freedom.
article.PVal: p = 0.008, same sentence as Outcome/SD (Results, 'Clinical outcomes').
article.SampleSize_NFinal: df = 8 on the reported t(8) = 3.477 implies n = 9. Matches the article's statement that 9 of 10 participants 'completed all follow-up assessments and are included in outcome analyses' (Results, 'Treatment exposure and follow-up') and the Figure 3 legend ('n = 9 at all other time points' after baseline).

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: All 14 elements are explicitly described. Comparator, randomization and blinding are each described as absent rather than present ('single-group, within-subjects design'; open-label psilocybin sessions; Discussion cites 'lack of a control group or blinding' as a limitation), which satisfies the described-including-as-absent rule. Setting is described via institutional affiliation (UNM Health Sciences Center) plus the detailed dosing-room description. Power is reported explicitly (n=10, power=0.803 to detect d=1.0). Harms and funding/COI each have dedicated sections.

article.RandomizationYN: Single-arm, open-label, within-subjects design (Methods, 'Study design'); no randomization was performed. Per the single-arm boundary rule, coded 0 (the element was absent), not 3.
article.BlindingYN: Open-label study; Discussion lists 'lack of a control group or blinding' as a limitation. Coded 0 per the single-arm boundary rule, not 3.
article.Double+Blind: Consistent with BlindingYN = 0; the study is open-label, not double-blind.
article.Comparator: No control or comparison arm; Discussion states 'lack of a control group' as a limitation. The two psilocybin sessions used different per-participant doses (0.3 mg/kg then up to 0.4 mg/kg) and subjective effects were compared between them (Table 1, paired t-tests df=5), but this is a within-subject dose-escalation across sequential sessions in one arm, not a between-groups or high-vs-low-dose comparator design, so Comparator remains 0.
article.PrimaryCare: No mention of primary-care settings or providers; conducted in a psychiatry department research clinic. The concept applies to a clinical trial in general, so coded 0 (absent) rather than 3.
article.Retention (%): Study is not randomized, so denominator is the enrolled/included sample. Figure 1 / Results 'Participants': 10 were 'included in the study' (received psilocybin); Results 'Treatment exposure and follow-up': 9 'completed all follow-up assessments.' Retention = 9/10 x 100 = 90.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1 on substantive-discussion grounds rather than statistical adjustment: no formal confound adjustment was performed (no control group), but the Discussion explicitly names candidate confounds -- 'it is not possible to separate unequivocally the effects of attention, psychosocial treatment, and time; expectancy effects related to knowledge of receiving psilocybin; and the specific effects of psilocybin.'
article.BaseStatus: No DSM-5-style severity specifier is given (study used DSM-IV, which has no built-in severity grading for dependence). Inferred 'Moderate' from an informal DSM-5 criterion-count crosswalk (2-3 mild, 4-5 moderate, 6+ severe) applied to the reported mean of 5.0 (SD 1.2, range 3-7) endorsed dependence-type criteria (Results, 'Participants'); this sits at the moderate end of that crosswalk. 8/10 participants also showed physical dependence (tolerance or withdrawal). Flagged as an inference, not an author-assigned label.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Results, 'Participants': 'Two participants were Native American/Alaska Native, one was African American, four were Hispanic, and three were white non-Hispanic.' Non-white/BIPOC = 2 + 1 + 4 = 7 of 10 = 70%. Hispanic is reported here as a category distinct from white non-Hispanic in the article's own breakdown, so no double-counting ambiguity.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 1 on reported income data alone (mean household income $47,023, SD $35,262; employment status also reported), per the field's 'income reported' example. Not an explicit low-income eligibility criterion -- this is descriptive demographic reporting, not a design feature targeting low-SES participants.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0. Figure 1 shows a highly selective funnel: 70 screened, 51 excluded before consent (11 exclusionary psychiatric/drug-use disorder, 9 lifetime hallucinogen use >10 occasions, 5 exclusionary medications, 4 exclusionary medical conditions, 3 age>65, etc.), plus 9 more excluded after consent, leaving 10 of 70 (14%) enrolled. A narrowly screened volunteer sample typical of an early-phase proof-of-concept trial, not reflective of a broader real-world treatment-seeking population.
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: Breath Alcohol Concentration was measured at each visit but the article explicitly states it 'was used to ensure safety of treatment and validity of assessments rather than as an outcome measure' (Methods, 'Substance use and consequences'). Labs/ECG/vitals were collected for screening and session-safety monitoring, not analyzed longitudinally as a physical/biological treatment outcome. Coded 0; flagged as a judgment call given the overlap between safety monitoring and outcome measurement.
article.Followup in months: Article reports duration only in weeks, structured throughout in 4-week blocks (weeks 1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-24, 25-36) built on the '12-week...intervention'; total follow-up is 'a total of 36 weeks' (Methods, 'Study design'; longest window is 'Weeks 25-36'). Converted using the article's own 4-week unit: 36 / 4 = 9 months. No separate end-of-treatment-only horizon is reported apart from this overall window.
article.CessationMeasured: Coded 1 based on the Abstract's explicit abstinence framing: 'Abstinence did not increase significantly in the first 4 weeks of treatment... but increased significantly following psilocybin administration.' The underlying instrument (TLFB) yields percent drinking/abstinent days rather than a discrete binary cessation rate, so this is a judgment call that the article's own abstinence language qualifies as a cessation-type outcome, distinct from the partial-reduction outcome (percent heavy drinking days) captured under ReductionMeasured.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 0. TLFB tracks daily drinking continuously, which could in principle reveal a return to use, but the article never names or reports a distinct relapse rate or relapse-tracking outcome.
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 1 on two grounds: (1) MET session fidelity was formally coded with the Motivational Interviewing Treatment Integrity system (MITI 3.1) and benchmarked against a proficiency threshold (Results, 'Treatment exposure and follow-up'); (2) the Discussion states the study 'clearly demonstrat[es] feasibility' as one of its own framings of the findings.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Counted the 4 events in the dedicated 'Treatment-related adverse events' results subsection (headache, nausea/emesis, diarrhea, insomnia). A separate finding -- modest, transient, statistically significant blood-pressure elevation during dosing (Results, 'Acute effects') -- was not added as a 5th event: it is reported as an expected monitored physiologic parameter in a different subsection, not adjudicated by the authors as an adverse event, and the AE subsection itself confirms 'No participant required medication or other intervention for blood pressure.' Flagged as a borderline inclusion call.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: The article reports per-AE-type counts (5 headache, 1 nausea/emesis, 1 diarrhea, 1 insomnia) but never states a total number of distinct participants with >=1 AE, and overlap between these groups (e.g., whether the insomnia participant also had headache) is not addressed. A summed or de-duplicated total would require an unsupported assumption, so coded '.'.
article.AE_denominator: AEs were 'collected on an AE case report form at the end of the psilocybin sessions and at all subsequent visits' (Methods, 'Safety assessment') for all participants who received psilocybin; 10 completed the first psilocybin session (Figure 1) and were subject to this monitoring.

ae_events.Bogenschutz 2015_AE01: Graded Mild via rubric (not author CTCAE/SAE): transient, resolved within 24 hours, consistent with the cited Johnson et al. (2012) report of dose-dependent transient headache -- hence Onset 'post-session-acute'. InterventionRequired coded '.' rather than inferred 'N': the article's blanket no-intervention sentence ('No participant required medication or other intervention for blood pressure, anxiety, or other psychiatric symptoms') does not name headache specifically.
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2015_AE02: Single transient episode of nausea/emesis during dosing, no reported escalation or complication; graded Mild via rubric. InterventionRequired coded '.' because the article's blanket no-intervention statement covers only blood pressure/anxiety/psychiatric symptoms, not GI events, and no antiemetic use is mentioned either way.
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2015_AE03: Diarrhea in a participant with pre-existing irritable bowel syndrome, occurring during one session only; graded Mild via rubric given no reported complication, hospitalization, or persistence. InterventionRequired coded '.' for the same reason as AE02 (not covered by the article's blanket statement).
ae_events.Bogenschutz 2015_AE04: Single-night insomnia following a session, no reported persistence beyond that night; graded Mild via rubric (persistence of days-to-weeks would move it to Moderate). Onset coded 'post-session-acute'. InterventionRequired coded '.' as not addressed by the article's blanket no-intervention statement, which names only blood pressure/anxiety/psychiatric symptoms.

config_proposal.note: d derived as t/sqrt(n) = 3.477/sqrt(9) = 1.159 from the primary designated contrast (baseline vs. weeks 5-12 percent heavy drinking days, paired t(8)=3.477, n=9). This treats a within-subjects paired statistic as an input to a between-groups conversion pipeline, which is the textbook 'approx' scenario named in this prompt's Step 4. It does not exactly reproduce the authors' own Morris-Deshon-corrected Cohen's d values in Figure 3, which are reported for different sub-window splits (weeks 5-8 and weeks 9-12 separately, not the combined 5-12 window used in the text's primary analysis) -- those range 1.109 and 0.869 respectively, bracketing this derived value and supporting its plausibility without matching it exactly.
